jobs.title: Technical Project Manager - Remote Work
jobs.description:
At BairesDev®, we've been leading the way in technology projects for over 15 years. We deliver cutting-edge solutions to giants like Google and the most innovative startups in Silicon Valley.

Our diverse 4,000+ team, composed of the world's Top 1% of tech talent, works remotely on roles that drive significant impact worldwide.

When you apply for this position, you're taking the first step in a process that goes beyond the ordinary. We aim to align your passions and skills with our vacancies, setting you on a path to exceptional career development and success.

Technical Project Manager at BairesDev

Lead technical projects from planning through delivery while ensuring alignment between technical teams and business objectives. This role focuses on managing project lifecycles, coordinating cross-functional teams, and applying both technical knowledge and project management expertise to drive successful outcomes.

What You'll Do:

- Plan, execute, and monitor technical projects ensuring on-time delivery within scope and budget.
- Coordinate cross-functional teams including developers, designers, and stakeholders.
- Manage project risks, dependencies, and timelines while maintaining clear communication.
- Facilitate agile ceremonies and ensure teams follow best practices for project delivery.
- Track project progress and provide regular updates to stakeholders and leadership.
- Bridge technical and business perspectives to ensure successful project outcomes.

What We Are Looking For:

- 3+ years of experience in technical project management or related roles.
- Strong understanding of software development processes and technical concepts.
- Experience with agile methodologies and project management tools.
- Proven ability to manage multiple projects and prioritize competing demands.
- Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
- Advanced level of English.

How we do make your work (and your life) easier:

- 100% remote work (from anywhere).
- Excellent compensation in USD or your local currency if preferred
- Hardware and software setup for you to work from home.
- Flexible hours: create your own schedule.
- Paid parental leaves, vacations, and holidays.
- Innovative and multicultural work environment: collaborate and learn from the global Top 1% of talent.
- Supportive environment with mentorship, promotions, skill development, and diverse growth opportunities.

Apply now and become part of a global team where your unique talents can truly thrive!

jobs.title: Chef de projet senior / Senior, Project Manager -Hybrid -Quebec City, Quebec, Canada
jobs.description:
Job Description

Présente partout au Canada, Pario Ingénierie et sciences de l’environnement LP est une firme spécialisée de services-conseils en ingénierie judiciaire, en sciences de l’environnement et en assainissement, reconnue comme un chef de file auprès des clients des secteurs de l’assurance et de la gestion des risques.

Nous avons actuellement un poste de Chef/Cheffe de projets à pourvoir au sein de notre équipe de Québec. La personne retenue soutiendra nos activités en croissance au Québec, qui offrent des services de sciences de l’environnement et de gestion de projets aux marchés de l’assurance et de la gestion des risques. Le poste consiste à collaborer avec les clients et les membres de l’équipe afin de diriger les travaux d’atténuation des déversements, de délimitation, d’assainissement et de documentation nécessaires au nettoyage des sites et à la fermeture des dossiers.

Exigences du poste :

Diplôme universitaire en sciences ou en génie (de préférence en environnement ou en sciences de la Terre), ou diplôme connexe assorti d’une expérience pertinente.
Au moins cinq années d’expérience dans le domaine de l’environnement, dont au moins une année en gestion de projets.

Expérience de projets d’assainissement des sols et des eaux souterraines, notamment en délimitation, en surveillance et en gestion.
Expérience dans la sélection et la direction de sous-traitants.
Expérience en facturation, en budgétisation et dans d’autres volets de la gestion de projets.
Capacité démontrée à gérer et à diriger efficacement le personnel de terrain.
Excellentes aptitudes à communiquer oralement et par écrit en français; une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais constitue un atout.
Expérience en communication avec les clients, les organismes de réglementation et les autres parties prenantes.
Permis de conduire valide et disponibilité pour se déplacer dans la province de Québec.

Milieu et conditions de trava il

Nous accueillons et encourageons les candidatures de personnes en situation de handicap. Des mesures d’adaptation sont offertes sur demande aux personnes candidates tout au long du processus de recrutement et d’évaluation.

Déclaration concernant les démarches non sollicitées — Agences de recrutement

Nous n’acceptons pas les candidatures non sollicitées transmises par des tiers recruteurs et demandons aux agences de ne pas communiquer directement avec nos employés ou nos gestionnaires pour leur présenter des candidats. Veuillez noter que nous ne verserons aucuns frais pour un placement découlant de la réception d’un curriculum vitæ non sollicité et que tout curriculum vitæ ainsi transmis sera considéré comme de l’information publique. Nous acceptons volontiers les curriculum vitæ soumis directement par les personnes candidates.

With offices across Canada, Pario Engineering & Environmental Sciences LP is a niche forensic engineering, environmental science, and remediation consulting firm that is a leader in providing services to insurance and risk management clients.

We have an existing opening for a Project Manager to join our Quebec City team. This position will support our growing Quebec operations, which provide environmental science and project management services to the insurance and risk management markets. The position will involve working with clients and team members to direct spill mitigation, delineation, remediation, and documentation to support clean ups and file closure.

Role Requirements:
Degree in Science or Engineering (Environmental or Earth Sciences preferred) or related diploma with applicable experience.
A minimum of 5 years’ experience within the environmental field with at least 1 year of project management experience.

Experience in soil and groundwater remediation projects including delineation, monitoring and management.
Experience retaining and directing subcontractors.
Experience with invoicing, budgeting, and other areas of project management.
Successfully managing and directing field staff is a must.
Strong verbal and written communication skills in French, strong English communication is an asset.
Experience communicating with clients, regulators and other involved stakeholders.
A valid driver's license and willingness to travel within the province of Quebec.

Environment/Work Conditions

We welcome and encourage applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates throughout the recruitment and assessment process.

Unsolicited Outreach Statement – Recruitment Agencies

We will not accept unsolicited resume submittals from third- party recruiters and hereby request agencies not to contact our employees or managers directly to present candidates. Be advised we will NOT pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume and will consider any unsolicited resumes forwarded public information. We welcome resumes submitted directly from candidates.

jobs.title: Commissioning Project Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

Since our inception, EEA Consulting Engineers has been committed to fostering an inclusive and sustainable workplace that focuses on the growth and success of our employees, a dedication that was further solidified when we transitioned to an Employee-Owned model nearly two decades ago. At EEA, we believe in empowering our Employee-Owners to thrive both professionally and personally, while nurturing strong connections with one another and our valued clients. Our unwavering support for our Employee-Owners has earned us recognition as a Top Workplace for over a decade. Our team consists of talented professionals including engineers, designers, and administrative professionals, spread across our three office locations. Join us and become a part of our thriving community of Employee-Owners!

We are seeking a Commissioning Project Manager
to play a key role in delivering high-performing building systems that meet design intent, operational goals, and client expectations. In this role, you’ll work closely with owners, design teams, contractors, and internal project teams to lead commissioning efforts across complex facilities, applying your technical expertise and problem-solving skills to improve building performance, reliability, and sustainability. Candidates must be based in the Albuquerque, New Mexico area or willing to travel frequently to the region.

Responsibilities

Lead commissioning activities for mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems across complex facilities, including laboratories, higher education, healthcare, municipal, and mission-critical environments
Manage and coordinate commissioning activities from pre-design through post-occupancy, establishing project strategy, scope, and performance objectives
Develop and execute commissioning plans, schedules, and functional test procedures for HVAC and specialty systems in alignment with project requirements and industry standards
Monitor project progress, timelines, and milestones, providing clear status updates and documentation for internal and client teams
Support development of commissioning scopes, fee proposals, and project execution strategies in collaboration with senior leadership
Review construction documents, specifications, submittals, and system designs to identify commissioning requirements, risks, and potential issues
Perform site inspections, system readiness evaluations, and functional performance testing to verify installation quality, integration, and operational performance
Analyze test results, troubleshoot system issues, and recommend corrective actions to optimize performance
Collaborate with owners, architects/engineers, contractors, and equipment vendors to resolve technical challenges and achieve project objectives
Support owner training, systems documentation, and final commissioning reports
Ensure commissioning activities align with industry standards, best practices, and sustainability requirements such as LEED or IECC

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Engineering, Construction, or a related field with at least 2 years of relevant field experience; or completion of a 2-year technical certificate program with 5 years of relevant field experience
Hands-on experience in HVAC or lighting controls, test and balance, commissioning, HVAC design, system start-up, or similar technical roles
Working knowledge of commissioning standards and guidelines, including ASHRAE, NEBB, or ACG (AABC Commissioning Group)
Strong understanding of commissioning processes, including pre-functional inspections, equipment start-up, and functional performance testing
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and technical documentation
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively across multidisciplinary teams and client-facing environments
Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a deadline-driven environment
Willingness to travel up to 50%

Desired Qualifications

Experience designing mechanical, electrical, or plumbing systems
Commissioning certifications (CxA, CCP, CBCP, or similar)
OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification
NICET certification
Experience with commissioning software such as BlueRithm or Facility Grid
Familiarity with LEED or IECC commissioning processes
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Bluebeam Revu

What We Offer

Annual merit increases based on work performance
Annual profit-sharing bonus, contingent on company performance
Low-cost medical, dental, and vision insurance plans. Medical coverage for individual employees is paid in full by EEA
ESOP (Employee Stock Ownership Plan) retirement account. EEA on average contributes 10% of an employee's salary into the ESOP Trust each year, at no cost to the employee!

401k with company match, available the first day of the next month following start date
$50,000 in Life Insurance at no cost to the employee
Short-Term and Long-Term Disability Coverage at no cost to the employee
Flexible working hours and hybrid schedule
Fun company events, outings, and happy hours
'Dress for Your Day' dress code

Company Brief

EEA Consulting Engineers is a premier Employee-Owned firm, providing comprehensive mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) consulting engineering services to diverse facilities across all market sectors. Established in 1977 in Austin, Texas as an energy conservation engineering consultant, EEA has since evolved into a leading MEP design firm offering a wide range of services including building commissioning, process utility engineering, utility master planning, and acoustics, noise, and vibration engineering. EEA has successfully completed projects nationally and internationally in both prime and sub-consultant roles and is licensed in all 50 states and the District of Columbia.

As a Top Workplace and MEP Giant, we prioritize our employees' satisfaction by fostering a collaborative, adaptable, and enjoyable work environment, guided by our core values of Flexibility, Integrity, Excellence, Sustainability, Transparency, and Accountability.

5+ years of project management experience in an engineering environment
Familiarity with project management tools and processes
Strong organizational and communication skills

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Safety
jobs.description:
Join the team bringing autonomy to the built world

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.

About The Role

This is Bedrock's first dedicated Safety Technical Program Manager
, a role built to establish the execution structure that lets us roll out new autonomy capabilities quickly without compromising safety rigor. As we scale to new machine types and expanded operational domains, we are evolving our safety practices toward more explicit, strategic execution.

You will own program execution for the safety, systems engineering, and state estimation work that makes autonomous heavy equipment safe to operate in the real world. This is a hands-on individual contributor role driving alignment and delivery across engineering, safety, autonomy, hardware, and field operations through influence, structure, and clear communication. You will be the connective tissue between safety strategy and technical delivery, making sure requirements are traceable, dependencies are visible, and risks surface early enough to act on. We are a startup that values agility. We believe that speed and safety are compatible when the traceability behind them is solid.

What You'll Do

Own planning and strategic execution for the safety and systems portions of the autonomy roadmap, from requirements through validated field deployment.
Support safety requirements being traceable, reusable across platforms and sites, and integrated into roadmaps from inception, partnering with safety and systems engineering on hazard analysis, validation evidence, and release readiness.
Build and maintain the validation plan spanning simulation and on-site testing, ensuring system-level changes are verified before they reach customers.
Map and actively manage dependencies and tradeoffs across systems, hardware, software, state estimation, and safety, weighing safety impact alongside schedule impact and identifying single points of failure on the critical path before they slip.
Drive program reviews, risk, and change management for multi-disciplinary, safety-critical initiatives, and provide reporting on roadmap health, delivery status, and safety implications clear enough to support both executive decisions and customer-facing discussions.
Translate field signals into prioritized engineering work and tracking issues to resolution.

What You'll Bring

7+ years of technical program management experience, including 2+ years leading programs involving safety-critical or high-integrity systems.
Domain experience in robotics, autonomous systems, aerospace, or another physical-world safety-critical domain, with a working understanding of the software, firmware, and hardware stacks behind real-world autonomy.
Working familiarity with a functional safety standard, such as ISO 26262 or IEC 61508, and how it shapes program structure, evidence, and release gates.
Enough working fluency in statistics and probability to interpret validation results and reliability metrics critically, not just track that they exist.
Understanding of the rigor, validation, and cross-functional coordination required to operate reliably in the physical world.
A track record of managing complex, cross-functional programs under ambiguity, taking systems from concept to production.
The ability to operate at a deep technical level and to distill complex risks and interdependencies into aligned, actionable plans for engineers and executives alike.
Strong dependency, risk, and change-management instincts in environments where safety and schedule are both non-negotiable.
A track record of thriving in fast-paced, high-ownership environments, with startup experience strongly preferred and a bias toward building structure that helps us scale through complexity.
Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.

jobs.description:
Brief Description

Projects do not deliver themselves, and in an enterprise IT environment the distance between a requirement and an award is where most programs lose time. The Red Gate Group is seeking a Project Manager
to support a major Intelligence Community customer, running projects end to end and driving acquisition records through their lifecycle so requirements become delivered capability on schedule.

As the Project Manager, you will plan, execute, and close projects that meet or exceed customer objectives. You will set clear and attainable project objectives, build project requirements, and manage the constraints of cost, time, scope, and quality. You will develop the overall project plan and run project operations day to day, managing stakeholders, the project team, risk, schedule, budget, and conflicts, making sure every team member knows and executes their role, keeping production schedules on track, using system resources effectively, and coordinating resolution when production problems surface. You will build the relationships between customers, teaming partners, and vendors that IT service delivery depends on.

You will also own the acquisition side of delivery. That means fully engaging stakeholders, from business managers and Contracting Officer Representatives to requirement owners and program managers, on requirements and the activities around them. You will create acquisition records and requisitions in customer systems, build out contract line item numbers, obtain and add funding to records, upload supporting documentation, and finalize records with the COR or requirement owner. You will review acquisition documentation for completeness, including statements of work, independent government cost estimates, market research, and justifications and approvals, track requirements records through their full lifecycle, respond to action items, and push recommendations through to timely award. Along the way you will manage all project and acquisition documentation, monitor acquisition status, keep dashboards current, and generate the weekly and monthly reporting metrics each record or project requires. If you like owning outcomes from requirement to award to delivery, this is the seat.

Join us. The mission runs on projects that finish.

You Have

8+ years of project management experience, including recent experience within the last 2 years. This experience requirement is firm and cannot be met through education or certifications.
Master's degree in a related field, or one of the following in its place: an Associate's degree in a related field and 4 additional years of relevant experience, a Bachelor's degree in a related field and 2 additional years of relevant experience, or 6 additional years of relevant experience. The additional years used in place of the degree are on top of the 8 year experience requirement above, not counted within it.
Experience planning, executing, and closing projects, including managing cost, schedule, scope, quality, risk, and stakeholders.
Experience supporting federal acquisition activities, including creating and tracking acquisition records, building contract line item numbers, managing funding actions, and reviewing acquisition documentation.
Experience engaging government stakeholders such as CORs, requirement owners, and program managers.
Experience maintaining dashboards and producing recurring status reporting and metrics.
Active TS/SCI clearance with CI Polygraph, or the ability to obtain a polygraph.

Nice If You Have

Experience supporting an Intelligence Community customer.
PMP or equivalent project management credential.
Experience with government acquisition or requirements management systems.
Familiarity with acquisition documentation standards, including SOW/SOR development, IGCEs, market research, and Justifications and Approvals.

Company Description

The Red Gate Group, founded in 2006, is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Company based in Chantilly, VA. As an SDVOSB, the Red Gate Group has established a reputation for delivering quality multi-tiered services in intelligence analysis, strategic planning, program management, policy development, operational design, and technology integration. RGG delivers high-quality, customer-centric solutions around the world—from the foxhole to the highest levels of Government. Our motto, "Making a Difference for Country and Client," reflects our deep commitment to national security and service excellence. As an employer of choice, we offer comprehensive benefits including flexible time off, 11 paid holidays, immediate 401(k) eligibility with a generous match, and full medical, dental, and vision coverage. Our employees enjoy 100% company-paid life insurance and disability benefits, along with professional development assistance for degrees and certifications. We foster a culture of growth and work-life balance, backed by our commitment to supporting both our clients' missions and our employees' success. Join our team and be part of an organization that values both service excellence and employee wellbeing.

Job Description

As an Intelligence Analyst at Rhombus Power, you will create impactful intelligence assessments on topics including foreign military activities, information operations, regional conflicts, and country stability to support U.S. and Allied national security decision making. Analysts will fuse Rhombus Power’s unique, AI-derived data with a spectrum of open-source information to create these products.

Our Intelligence Analysts routinely perform thorough research and analysis on global security topics guided by client intelligence needs. The outputs from these efforts are primarily conveyed through intelligence assessments written in accordance with U.S. Intelligence Community standards; however, Analysts also deliver tailored briefings for internal and external audiences on topics in their areas of responsibility.

Candidates must excel at collaborative work and must exhibit strong interpersonal skills, as all team efforts depend on working closely within the intelligence team and with other cross-functional teams. Candidates should be able to provide and receive feedback that enhances overall team outputs and the company’s proprietary AI features.

Successful candidates will be solution-oriented self-starters who are tech savvy, can identify problems and opportunities, and propose solutions in a dynamic and fast-paced environment. Flexibility and the ability to multitask and prioritize efforts are crucial due to the pace of global events and the sometimes rapidly evolving needs of our clients.

We are seeking a candidate with subject matter expertise on the Russian military, preferably with experience in a U.S. military or government intelligence role. The ideal candidate will have significant knowledge of Russian military capabilities, hybrid warfare, and information operations with an up-to-date understanding of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and the threat it poses to NATO countries. Candidates must have strong writing skills and be capable of producing a high volume of quality analytic assessments under tight deadlines and with minimal review.

If you do not have experience as an analyst in the U.S. Intelligence Community, a writing sample will be requested as part of your application for this role and is a requirement for consideration. All writing samples must be your own work and ideally will have been produced within the last 3 years. The sample should be between one and three pages in length and assess a geopolitical or international security-related topic.

Responsibilities

Identify impactful intelligence topics based on a detailed understanding of client intelligence needs and missions.
Produce high-quality intelligence assessments that answer our clients most important intelligence questions by following U.S. Intelligence Community intelligence analysis and writing standards.
Utilize Rhombus Power’s AI-informed intelligence capabilities and expert research skills to gather information that serves as the foundation of intelligence products.
Identify information gaps and work with the Model and Data Development team to acquire sources of information to bridge gaps.
Utilize structured analytic techniques to ensure team intelligence products meet the highest standards.
Brief finished intelligence products.
Support enhancement of Rhombus Power intelligence capabilities by providing feedback on existing features and supporting the development of new applications and features.
Serve as a subject matter expert on Russia with a focus on operations in Ukraine and threats to NATO.

Qualifications

Minimum of 5 (five) years’ analytic experience with subject matter expertise related to Russia and its military.
Analytic experience and training with the U.S. Intelligence Community or military are strongly desired.
At minimum, a BA or BS in International Affairs, Political Science, Economics, or a similar social science field. An advanced degree is desired.
Experience writing intelligence products tailored to answering key client intelligence questions.
Experience providing briefings on complex national security and international affairs topics.
Familiarity using and developing qualitative and quantitative analytical methodologies.
Intellectual curiosity and emotional intelligence.
We are seeking candidates who would be eligible for a DoD Secret or Top Secret security clearance. If you currently hold a clearance, please indicate the level and sponsoring agency.
Familiarity with data analysis, statistics, data science, big data manipulation, and coding (Python, etc.) is particularly welcome.

OT Cybersecurity Analyst

Description:

The OT Cybersecurity Analyst supports the Corpus Christi Automation Department in deploying, integrating, and sustaining OT cybersecurity capabilities across the refinery's control systems. The role leads technical execution of platform deployments, develops monitoring and response workflows, supports incident response, and helps build the procedures and training needed for long-term sustainment. The Analyst works closely with Automation, Operations, IT, and Corporate Cybersecurity and supports the site's role in the company's OT Cybersecurity program.

Key Responsibilities:

Lead technical deployment, commissioning, and integration of OT cybersecurity platforms, including Nozomi (passive detection, vulnerability identification, threat intelligence), SolarWinds (network management), XONA (secure remote access), Octave/Hexagon Integrity (asset inventory and configuration management), and secure file transfer (Axway).
Define monitoring strategy, alert tuning, baselines, and escalation paths for OT networks and control system assets.
Investigate and analyze alerts and anomalies; correlate across platforms to separate genuine threats from false positives and normal process behavior.
Serve in OT Cyber Support and OT Network Support roles under the OT Cyber Incident Response Plan (OT CIRP), including triage, evidence preservation, containment recommendations, and lessons learned.
Perform security architecture reviews and risk assessments of DCS, PLC, SIS, historian, and network infrastructure consistent with ISA/IEC 62443 and NIST guidance.
Support asset inventory, vulnerability, and patch-risk assessment for Honeywell (Experion/TPS), Emerson DeltaV, Rockwell, Triconex, and associated servers and workstations.
Develop and maintain procedures, standards, runbooks, and documentation; support Management of Change for cybersecurity-related modifications.
Coordinate with Corporate Cybersecurity on SIEM/log integration, threat intelligence, and enterprise standards.
Train and mentor Automation staff and the OT Cybersecurity Technician on platform use and procedures.
Report program status, metrics, and risks to the Automation Manager.

Required Qualifications:

5–10 years of experience in industrial control systems, automation, OT networking, or OT cybersecurity, with at least 3 years focused on OT/ICS cybersecurity.
Direct experience in refining, petrochemical, chemical, power generation, oil & gas, or similar continuous-process industrial operations.
Working knowledge of DCS, PLC, and SIS architectures and industrial protocols (e.g., Modbus, OPC/OPC UA, EtherNet/IP).
Hands-on experience deploying or administering at least one OT network monitoring or asset visibility platform (e.g., Nozomi, Claroty, Dragos, Industrial Defender, Tenable OT).
Understanding of network segmentation, Purdue model, firewalls, DMZs, switches, and Windows server/Active Directory in OT environments.
Familiarity with ISA/IEC 62443, NIST CSF, and NIST SP 800-82.
Valid TWIC (Transportation Worker Identification Credential) card at time of start.
Ability to work safely on-site in an operating refinery and communicate clearly with operators, engineers, and IT.

Preferred Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Security, or related field (equivalent experience accepted).
Certifications such as GICSP, GRID, ISA/IEC 62443 Cybersecurity Expert/Specialist, CISSP, or Security+.
Experience with Honeywell Experion/TPS and/or Emerson DeltaV.
Experience with Nozomi, SolarWinds, XONA, Axway, or PAS/Hexagon Integrity.
Experience supporting incident response, tabletop exercises, or regulated security programs (e.g., TSA, USCG MTSA).

Work Environment:

Work is performed at an operating petroleum refinery. Candidates must follow company safety, PPE, permitting, and Management of Change requirements and be able to work in operating units, control rooms, and equipment rooms.
This is a 100% on-site position at the Corpus Christi Refinery. Remote or hybrid work is not available.
Candidates must pass company and contractor-agency background, drug, and safety screening.
Normal schedule is day shift, Monday–Friday, with occasional after-hours or call-out support during incidents, outages, and turnarounds

jobs.title: Business Analyst
jobs.description:
About Us

At Alteva RCM, we're dedicated to helping healthcare providers thrive through expert revenue cycle management, strategic insight, and innovative solutions. We're always looking for passionate, driven professionals who want to make a meaningful impact, grow their careers, and be part of a collaborative team committed to excellence.

About Alteva RCM

Alteva RCM is a healthcare revenue cycle management company that partners with medical practices and surgical centers nationwide. We help providers operate more efficiently, strengthen revenue cycle operations, and navigate the complexity of today's healthcare environment.

We serve a wide range of specialties and operate at scale, with technology playing an important role in how we support clients and internal operations.

About the Role

As Alteva grows, more of our work depends on technology and operations teams understanding each other. Billing, dispute resolution, finance, client services, and technology all have different views of the same workflows, and the details often get lost between them.

The Business Analyst is the person who closes that gap. You will work between departments to understand how work is done, gather and document requirements, and make sure that what gets built matches what the business needs. You will partner closely with Product Leadership, the Project Manager, the Technical Lead, developers, and QA, and you will be the main voice of the business in the room when solutions are designed.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is curious about operations, comfortable with ambiguity, and able to turn long conversations into clear, buildable requirements.

What You'll Own

Requirements & Discovery

Lead discovery with stakeholders across departments through interviews, workshops, and walk-throughs of how work is really done today
Map current-state and future-state processes, and identify handoffs, manual steps, gaps, and opportunities for automation
Turn business needs into clear PRDs, functional specifications, user stories with acceptance criteria, business rules, and data requirements
Ask why before how: separate the real problem from the proposed solution, and help stakeholders prioritize

Cross-Department Alignment

Act as the main point of contact between operations and technology, so developers understand the business context and operations understand the technical constraints
Surface conflicting or overlapping requests across departments early, and facilitate decisions
Keep a clear record of decisions, assumptions, dependencies, and open questions
Triage and clarify new requests through our intake process before they reach development

Delivery Support

Work with developers and QA during the build to answer questions, clarify requirements, and review work against acceptance criteria
Plan and support user acceptance testing: write UAT scenarios, coordinate testers, track defects, and confirm stakeholder sign-off
Support release readiness and post-release validation to confirm each change delivers the intended outcome
Partner with the Project Manager on prioritization, sprint planning, and status for the work you have scoped

Data & Documentation

Analyze operational data using SQL, spreadsheets, and reporting tools to size problems, validate assumptions, and measure results
Keep requirements, process documentation, and business rules current and easy to find in our project and documentation tools (such as Jira, Confluence, and Notion)
Use AI tools to speed up documentation, summarization, and analysis, while checking the output for accuracy
Prepare concise updates for leadership and operational stakeholders

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 90 days, this person should help the team work with fewer surprises and less rework. Specifically:

Requirements are written down once, clearly, and the whole team refers to them
Departments know how to submit a request and what to expect next
Developers and QA get fewer late clarifications and conflicting instructions
UAT has defined scenarios and clear sign-off before release
Documentation is current and trusted by operations and technology

What We're Looking For

Required

3+ years as a Business Analyst, systems analyst, or similar role in a technology- or operations-heavy environment
Proven experience gathering requirements from non-technical stakeholders and turning them into specifications developers can build from
Experience writing user stories, acceptance criteria, functional specifications, and process flows
Working knowledge of Agile delivery and experience working directly with developers and QA
Strong written communication, with clear and concise documentation
Comfortable facilitating conversations across several departments, balancing competing priorities, and building consensus
Experience with Jira and a documentation tool such as Confluence or Notion
Working SQL or data analysis skills
Comfortable in a growing environment where processes are still being defined

Preferred

Background in healthcare, revenue cycle management, medical billing, claims, or denials and appeals
Familiarity with independent dispute resolution (IDR) or the No Surprises Act
Familiarity with healthcare data and transactions such as X12 EDI (270/271, 276/277, 835, 837), or payer portals
Experience with Salesforce or other enterprise CRM requirements
Experience with workflow automation, integrations, or API concepts
Experience with Power BI, Tableau, or similar reporting tools
Business analysis certification (such as CBAP or PMI-PBA)
Experience working with distributed or offshore teams

Pay Range: $90,000 USD - $110,000 USD

Benefits

Alteva RCM offers our employees a comprehensive benefits package, including health, dental, vision, employee assistance plan, paid family leave, short-term disability and life insurance. We also provide a 401(k) plan with employer match, flexible spending accounts, employee discount program and an employee referral program.

Experience building reports or saved searches inside an ERP or BI tool

Direct experience with NetSuite and its relevant modules
Basic SQL, or experience with BI tools such as Power BI or Tableau
Familiarity with integrations (CRM, e-commerce, payroll, banking) and how data flows between systems
Experience writing SOPs and training end users

jobs.description:
Brief Description

An enterprise IT organization delivers services to dozens of external mission partners on a reimbursable basis, and every dollar it recovers depends on three things: a valid support agreement, an accurate baseline of the services each partner actually receives, and an invoice that gets paid. The Red Gate Group is seeking a Program Analyst (Business Analyst)
to support the cost recovery and interagency agreements function of a major Intelligence Community customer. You will draft, coordinate, execute, and sustain support agreements, to include Memorandum of Agreements (MOAs) and Memorandum of Understanding (MOUs), and interagency agreement forms such as the Treasury 7600A) between the customer and the external organizations it serves. Maintain the agreement templates and priority list, monitor agreement ceilings as funding is consumed, and work with internal agreement managers, technical points of contact, and the invoicing team so that agreements are in place before funding transfers are sent or received. You will participate in the cost recovery working group and in annual and mid-point agreement reviews, and you will engage external customers directly to resolve dollar and preparer discrepancies and keep agreements current. Processes Military Interdepartmental Purchase Request (MIPR) packages, ensuring complete documentation, accurate financial data, and timely execution in support of year-end Chief Financial Officer (CFO) suspense requirements and coordinate with stakeholders to resolve MIPR-related issues, process revisions, reconcile funding records, and support timely fiscal year-end execution.

The analytical side of the role is where the senior designation earns its keep. You will reconcile each customer's inventory baseline against the services delivered, generate annual planning estimates that combine existing service baselines with new services and the annual rate increase, forecast cost growth in current agreements so incoming funding transfers can be processed on time, and help refine the cost and pricing models behind a fee-for-service framework. You will support quality control of operations and maintenance invoices, follow up with customers on delinquent reimbursements from prior fiscal years, coordinate with customers and applicable stakeholders to resolve outstanding actions, return excess funds when appropriate, and ensure timely completion of required financial closeout activities. You will be required to build and maintain reporting tools in MS Excel, Tableau, and a ServiceNow platform that shows leadership the status of every agreement and the funding moving through it. Government leads will look to you for strategic advice on how the agreements and cost recovery processes should evolve, and for process improvements that automate the workflow rather than add steps to it.

Must Have

12+ years of experience conducting program, financial, or business analysis in support of interagency agreements, cost recovery, reimbursable billing, budget execution, or resource management for a federal or Department of Defense organization, including recent experience within the last 2 years. This experience requirement is firm and cannot be met through education or certifications.
Master's degree in a related field, or one of the following in its place: an Associate's degree in a related field and 4 additional years of relevant experience, a Bachelor's degree in a related field and 2 additional years of relevant experience, or 6 additional years of relevant experience. The additional years used in place of the degree are on top of the 12 year experience requirement above, not counted within it. In plain terms: with a Master's you need 12 years, with a Bachelor's 14, with an Associate's 16, and with no degree 18.
Experience drafting, coordinating, and executing interagency support agreements (Memoranda of Agreement, Memoranda of Understanding, Treasury 7600A or equivalent) and processing the related funding transfers, including Military Interdepartmental Purchase Requests.
Experience building planning estimates, cost or pricing models, or invoices for IT or shared services, and reconciling customer baselines against the services actually delivered.
Advanced Excel skills for reconciliation, forecasting, and ceiling tracking, and experience producing dashboards or status reporting in Tableau, Power BI, or a comparable tool.
Experience engaging external customers and senior government leadership directly, including presenting findings and recommendations and resolving funding or billing discrepancies.
Active TS/SCI clearance with current Counterintelligence (CI) Polygraph.

Nice If You Have

Experience with ServiceNow customer service management or invoicing modules.
Experience supporting agency comptrollers or Component Acquisition Office, (CAO) processes for incoming and outgoing funds transfers, including Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution.
Experience automating cost recovery, invoicing, or agreements workflows, or defining requirements for a development team that does.

WHAT IS THE OPPORTUNITY?

The role of the Project Manager is to plan, execute, and finalize Bank projects according to timelines, milestone events and within budget. Dans le cadre d'une mission auprès de l'un de nos clients, un grand groupe bancaire international, vous interviendrez en tant que Business Analyst MOA senior pour concevoir et déployer un cadre de contrôle réglementaire unifié couvrant EMIR, SFTR et MiFID II.

Le contexte fonctionnel

La mission s'inscrit dans un périmètre de reporting réglementaire couvrant les régimes EU et UK, au croisement des fonctions Compliance, métiers et IT. Elle porte sur la structuration et le déploiement d'un cadre de contrôle transverse, dans un environnement soumis à des exigences réglementaires multiples et en évolution constante.

Le besoin

La mission requiert la conception et le déploiement d'un cadre de contrôle unifié couvrant EMIR Refit, SFTR et MiFID II sur les périmètres EU et UK. Le consultant prendra en charge l'analyse fonctionnelle complète, depuis l'état des lieux jusqu'à la conception des contrôles, en passant par la rédaction des spécifications fonctionnelles, la coordination des tests UAT et le suivi post-déploiement. Un niveau senior est attendu, capable de piloter l'analyse métier, de maintenir la traçabilité exigences-contrôles-tests et d'assurer le transfert opérationnel dans les règles de l'art.

Vos missions

Analyse de l'existant et conception du cadre de contrôle cible pour les régimes de reporting réglementaire EU et UK (EMIR, SFTR, MiFID II)
Animation d'ateliers avec les équipes SME, IT, métiers et Compliance pour documenter les exigences, décisions et dépendances
Rédaction des spécifications fonctionnelles et des critères d'acceptation à destination des équipes IT, avec maintien de la traçabilité exigences-contrôles-tests
Coordination des tests fonctionnels et UAT, consolidation des preuves de test et suivi des défauts jusqu'à résolution
Pilotage de la période d'hypercare post-déploiement, production des rapports de stabilisation et préparation du transfert opérationnel

L'environnement

Domaines : reporting réglementaire, compliance, risque opérationnel, transaction reporting, trade reporting

Réglementaire : EMIR Refit, SFTR, MiFID II, périmètres EU et UK

Le consultant

Formation Bac+5 — Master 2 ou école d'ingénieur, idéalement avec une spécialisation en finance. Une expérience confirmée en business analysis MOA réglementaire est indispensable, avec une maîtrise avérée du regulatory reporting, de la compliance et des réglementations EMIR et MiFID II. La mission exige une solide pratique de la rédaction de functional specifications, du gap analysis, du requirements management, de la workshop facilitation, de la coordination de tests UAT et de la production de SOP documentation. La capacité à assurer un hypercare support structuré et un operational handover rigoureux est également requise. Apprécié : expérience sur SFTR, connaissance des exigences AMF, pratique de la data quality, de la data governance et de l'exception management.

Act as a key analytical partner by translating business questions into structured insights and recommendations.

Experience as a Business Analyst or Data Analyst, preferably in a revenue-focused environment.
Knowledge of the Media and Advertising landscape.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret complex datasets.
Proficiency with Looker or equivalent BI tools and strong Excel skills.

Clear communication skills and a detail‑oriented mindset.

Fluency in English and French.

At Alstom, we understand transport networks and what moves people. From high-speed trains, metros, monorails, and trams, to turnkey systems, services, infrastructure, signalling and digital mobility, we offer our diverse customers the broadest portfolio in the industry. Every day, more than 80 000 colleagues lead the way to greener and smarter mobility worldwide, connecting cities as we reduce carbon and replace cars.

Purpose of the job:

As part of the Global People Analytics & Governance team, you will help turn HR data into forward-looking insights that support workforce and business decisions. You will contribute to predictive and scenario-based workforce analytics, enrich strategic dashboards, and help shape data and AI use cases that anticipate future skills, capacity, retention, and organisational needs This internship offers international exposure to Workforce Analytics, Data Visualization, Business Intelligence, and the application of Artificial Intelligence in HR.

Organisation structure

Human Resources department/People analytics and Efficiency & Data intelligence

Reports directly to: Global People Analytics & Governance Director

Key Responsibilities:

HR Data Analytics, Forecasting and Reporting
Produce monthly and quarterly HR reports.
Consolidate global HR metrics and workforce indicators.
Develop forward-looking workforce analyses, including trends, forecasts and scenarios, to anticipate future skills, capacity, attrition and organisational needs.
Support recurring workforce analyses.
Check data consistency and quality before publication.
Identify opportunities to streamline and automate reporting processes .
Data Visualization and Dashboards
Contribute to the enhancement of existing Qlik solutions.
Support the development and improvement of current dashboards.
Design visualizations tailored to HR and management needs.
Improve the usability and effectiveness of reporting solutions .
Preparing Future Analytics and AI Use Cases
Participate in identifying new user and business requirements.
Structure datasets for future analyses.
Build and test advanced analytics use cases—such as forecasting, segmentation, scenario modelling and leading indicators—and translate their outputs into actionable recommendations for HR and business leaders.
Contribute to experiments involving Generative AI applied to HR.
Recommend improvements to reporting and analytics practices.

Educational Requirements

Mandatory:

Currently pursuing a Master’s degree (Bac+4/Bac+5) in Data Analytics, Business Analytics, Data Science, Statistics, Information Systems, or a related field. Power BI, QlikCloud

Fluency in English; any other language skills will be of advantage

Desirable:

Basic knowledge of SQL, Power Query, Python, or Workforce Analytics

Competencies & Skills

Strong analytical mindset and curiosity.
Rigor and attention to detail.
Ability to communicate and simplify analytical findings for non-technical audiences.
Ability to work with increasing autonomy.
Strong interpersonal skills and professional English.

Key competences

Data driven – uses facts and insights to improve decisions and performance
Business oriented – understands how HR contributes to the business value
Improvement mindset- continuously challenges complexity and looks for better optimised ways of working
Digital mindset – actively explores technology, automation and AI opportunities
Collaborative – builds strong partnership across HR and other functions
Result oriented – turns analysis and ideas into measurable improvements

jobs.title: Donor Communications Program Manager, California
jobs.description:
Application Instructions

Please note that the application period ends at 12:00 am Eastern Time on the due date listed. For applicants in Pacific Time
, please plan to submit your application by 8:59pm
the day before.

Although cover letters are not required, we appreciate and will consider a letter explaining your interest in this position and our organization. (You can upload the cover letter in the same location as your resume.)

Internal applicants (TNC employees) must apply through Workday via the Jobs Hub.

What We Can Achieve Together

The Donor Communications Program Manager develops and manages the workflow of various donor-facing products within the California Chapter’s Donor Communications Team. The Program Manager is responsible for developing project timelines; tracking assignments across the team; facilitating meetings to ensure deliverable completion and submission; and managing a robust deliverable calendar, which outlines the workstream for major communication products for TNC’s principal gift, corporate, foundation, individual, and emerging major donors. This is a highly collaborative role and requires someone who can engage with all levels of staff.

Essential Functions

The Donor Communications Program Manager is a key connector within the team and across TNC. The main objectives of the position include but are not limited to:

Managing the Product Workflow and Deliverable Calendar: The Program Manager will manage the product workflow through a deliverable calendar and solve any problems related to product development. These products may include concept notes, proposals, reports, newsletters, board documents, membership mailings, campaign materials, and strategy briefs targeted to TNC’s principal gift, corporate, foundation and individual donors. The Program Manager will facilitate meetings to understand product needs and update the editorial calendar as new products come into the pipeline. They will develop project plans and timelines to ensure that Conservation, Science, Development, and Finance teams are aligned on product needs and that the given deliverable is submitted on time and per the donor’s guidelines.
Providing Operational and Strategic Support to the Donor Communications Team: The Program Manager organizes products on internal sharing platforms to improve internal communications between Development, Science, Conservation, and Finance staff, and to maximize the utilization and re-purposing of key donor materials. The Program Manager must be an expert in the systems and resources used by the team and apply that knowledge to create efficient processes for managing workflow. They will develop documentation, modify processes, and participate in the enhancement of systems and tools used by the team. They will also support the team in strategic planning.

The Program Manager works in close collaboration with any or all of the following: TNC staff, donors, volunteers, vendors, financial institutions, legal professionals, and contractors. They will provide advice, recommendations, and training related to the functional area of the team. They will manage diverse tasks, evaluate alternatives, project outcomes, and implement solutions in order to improve effectiveness, consulting with leadership as needed. They must be responsive to deadlines and work well under pressure.

Responsibilities & Scope

Manage and implement multiple projects, including managing deliverable calendar, setting deadlines, and ensuring accountability.
Act independently and in supervisor’s stead as needed, exercising independent judgment to identify and solve problems.
Demonstrate sensitivity in handling confidential information.
Effectively communicate across departments and chapters within the global organization.
Develop and implement new processes that will ensure department- and organization-wide goals and strategies are achieved.
Ensure programmatic commitments, TNC policies and procedures, financial standards, and legal requirements are met and managed for compliance.
Travel occasionally, work long and flexible hours as needed.
Work environment involves only infrequent exposure to disagreeable elements and minor physical exertion and/or strain.
Work is diversified and may not always fall under established practices and guidelines.

We’re Looking For You

Are you looking for a career to help people and nature? Guided by science, TNC creates innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that people and nature can thrive together. We’re looking for someone who is a highly collaborative and detail oriented project manager. Come join TNC and apply today!

What You’ll Bring

Bachelor’s degree and 3 years of related experience (or equivalent combination of education and experience).
Experience coordinating projects.
Experience generating reports and analyzing and interpreting data.
Experience with current technology in relevant field.
Experience working across departments.
Experience, coursework, or other training in principles and practices of relevant field.

Desired Qualifications

Multi-lingual skills and multi-cultural or cross-cultural experience appreciated.
Ability to implement complex processes.
Ability to use existing technology to achieve desired results.
Demonstrated experience using diplomacy and tact to build strong relationships and motivate staff.
Experience interpreting guidelines to achieve desired results.
Experience supervising staff, interns and/or volunteers.
Experience with database management.
Knowledge of current trends in the specific field.
Strong organization and negotiating skills, accuracy, attention to detail and ability to manage multiple tasks.
Successful experience implementing strategic program goals.
Understanding of basic accounting principles.

Salary Information

The starting annual pay for this position is within the range of $72,384 - $92,925
. This range only applies to candidates whose country of employment is the USA and state of employment is California. More specific ranges based the location of the TNC office this position would use as a secondary or primary location are:

Sacramento, San Diego, Ventura, and most locations in CA: $72,384 - $85,300

LA County and the San Francisco Bay Area: $79,100 - $92,925

Where a successful candidate’s pay will fall within this range will be based on a variety of factors, including location, qualifications, skills, and experience. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment.

Who We Are

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube to hear stories from staff or visit Glassdoor.

One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”

What We Bring

Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

TNC offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package including health care benefits, flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) plan with an 8% employer match, parental leave, accrued paid time off, life insurance, disability coverage, employee assistance program, other life and work well-being benefits. Learn more about our Benefits and Perks here.

We’re proud to offer a flexible work environment that supports of the health and well-being of the people we employ.

Our recruiting process includes a rolling interview process to ensure we engage applicants in a timely manner. This means we may review applications in the order in which they are received. Once a strong candidate pool is identified, the role will be unposted. The timeline may vary depending on the expressed interest in the role, so we highly encourage candidates to apply as soon as possible.

Employees must submit their application by logging into Workday and applying via the Jobs Hub.

The Nature Conservancy is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
Our commitment to equal employment opportunity includes the recognition that our conservation mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people of all backgrounds, beliefs, and culture. Recruiting and mentoring staff to create an inclusive organization is a priority, and we encourage applicants from all cultures, races, colors, religions, sexes, national or regional origins, ages, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, military, protected veteran status or other status protected by law.

The successful applicant must meet the requirements of The Nature Conservancy's background screening process.

Do you have military experience? Visit our U.S. Military Skills Translator to match your military experience with our current job openings!

TNC is committed to offering accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application process. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please send a note to applyhelp@tnc.org with Request for Accommodation in the subject line.

jobs.description:
You will own enablement programs that help every team at Kiteworks do their best work. You will work across functions, from Engineering, Product, and Marketing to Customer Success, Support, Finance, People, and Operations, and you will treat each team as a client with its own needs.

You will work as a program owner and internal consultant. You will find where teams are stuck, design the right learning or change program, bring in the right experts, run it from start to finish, and measure whether it worked. You will build repeatable programs that scale as the company grows, so we are not rebuilding training from scratch each time.

What you'll do

Own company-wide onboarding so every new hire, in every function and location, ramps quickly and has a consistent experience.
Partner with leaders across the company to find skill gaps, readiness needs, and adoption challenges, then turn them into prioritized enablement programs.
Plan, launch, and continuously improve programs from scoping through delivery and measurement, including role-based learning paths, certifications, and readiness checkpoints for any team.
Run enablement for company-wide moments such as product launches, policy and process changes, tool rollouts, and organizational changes.
Support manager and leadership development in partnership with People and Partners.
Drive adoption of AI tools and AI-native ways of working. Build practical training that helps people at every level use them well in their own roles.
Work with subject matter experts across the company to turn their knowledge into clear, usable learning content.
Manage the learning platform and content library so materials are current, easy to find, and accurate.
Own the enablement calendar and communications so employees know what is coming, why it matters, and how to take part.
Define and track program metrics such as time to productivity, completion rates, adoption, and business impact. Report results to leadership and adjust based on what the data shows.
Collect feedback from employees and managers, and use it to decide what to build, change, or retire.
Keep many concurrent projects on schedule across teams with different priorities and working styles.

What you'll bring

Required
4+ years in enablement, learning and development, organizational development, or a closely related role.
2+ years of hands-on program management, including running full program lifecycles.
A track record of building and delivering programs that changed behavior and results for more than one type of team or audience.
Experience with an LMS or learning platform, and with the collaboration and business systems teams use day to day.
Practical experience using AI tools to automate work or improve learning programs.
Clear, direct written and verbal communication, and the ability to work with senior leaders and technical experts.
Strong organization and follow-through across competing priorities.

Preferred
Experience supporting both technical and non-technical teams in the same organization.
Experience with change management or internal communications for company-wide rollouts.
Experience building assessment, coaching, or certification programs.
Experience in technology, security, compliance, or another regulated industry.
Experience in a high-growth company with a distributed team.

Success in the first 12 months

New hires in every function ramp faster, with clear readiness gates and a consistent experience.
Enablement programs are live and measured for at least four functions across the company.
Teams across the company adopt key tools and AI workflows, and can show the results.
Leaders get a regular, trusted view of program results.
Employees and managers say enablement is useful, easy to find, and easy to use.

Execution – We deliver results with focus, ownership, and consistency. Our teams take initiative, solve challenges proactively, and continuously optimize how we work to create meaningful impact for our customers.
Transparency – We communicate openly and clearly, ensuring stakeholders have the information they need to make informed decisions. We foster a culture of trust, welcome feedback, and embrace accountability in everything we do.
Integrity – We uphold the highest standards of honesty and responsibility. Our teams act ethically, consistently honor commitments, and build trust through principled, reliable actions.

Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

We’re looking for a talented and energetic Accounts Receivable Operation Analyst to join our accounting operations team. You will interact and coordinate with colleagues in Accounting, Finance, Treasury, Tax and various other departments across Robinhood to meet daily operational needs. This position will be responsible for increasing efficiency by accurately processing all receivable transactions and meeting associated deadlines. The Accounts Receivable Analyst will gain exposure to the global, technical and operational receivable activities and have a high degree of commitment, independent, resourcefulness, and detail-oriented to achieve 100% accuracy.

This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA, New York, NY or Chicago, IL office(s), with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week.

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What You’ll Do

Manage full-cycle billing operations, generating timely invoices and customer statements while maintaining accurate accounts receivable records.
Drive end-to-end management of outstanding balances through rigorous account reconciliations, variance analysis, cash application, and proof-of-delivery validation.
Achieve key AR performance metrics by proactively driving collections and managing resolution plans for delinquent accounts.
Deliver high-touch, solutions-driven support to customers, cultivating strong relationships by resolving billing inquiries and payment discrepancies efficiently.
Provide actionable updates and visibility to internal leadership regarding account statuses and resolution timelines.
Contribute to the development and implementation of scalable AR processes, tools, and platforms to enhance operational productivity.
Identify, evaluate, and integrate AI-driven automation tools to optimize cash application, invoice matching, and routine AR workflows.
Operate with a high degree of ownership and urgency to consistently hit deadlines, manage ad-hoc initiatives, and deliver high-impact results.

What You Bring

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
Minimum 2–3 years of relevant AR experience in the tech industry or a comparable fast-paced, complex environment.
Collaborative team player who builds strong cross-functional partnerships across the organization.
Hands-on experience with Oracle ERP (or a comparable system).
Highly organized, deadline-driven, and capable of processing and managing a high volume of transactions with strict accuracy.
A professional who can work independently with minimal supervision and effectively manage their time to meet all deadlines.
Strong attention to detail, ability to multitask, and a drive to learn and grow.
Intermediate Excel skills (including v-lookups, pivot tables, and basic data analysis).
Familiarity with or a strong eagerness to adopt AI-driven financial tools and automations to enhance AR operations.

What We Offer

Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career.
Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching.
Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents.
Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds.
Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not.
Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more.
Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits.
Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more!
Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces.

Job Description

Présente partout au Canada, Pario Ingénierie et sciences de l’environnement LP est une firme spécialisée de services-conseils en ingénierie judiciaire, en sciences de l’environnement et en assainissement, reconnue comme un chef de file auprès des clients des secteurs de l’assurance et de la gestion des risques.

Nous avons actuellement un poste de Chef/Cheffe de projets à pourvoir au sein de notre équipe de Québec. La personne retenue soutiendra nos activités en croissance au Québec, qui offrent des services de sciences de l’environnement et de gestion de projets aux marchés de l’assurance et de la gestion des risques. Le poste consiste à collaborer avec les clients et les membres de l’équipe afin de diriger les travaux d’atténuation des déversements, de délimitation, d’assainissement et de documentation nécessaires au nettoyage des sites et à la fermeture des dossiers.

Exigences du poste :

Diplôme universitaire en sciences ou en génie (de préférence en environnement ou en sciences de la Terre), ou diplôme connexe assorti d’une expérience pertinente.
Au moins cinq années d’expérience dans le domaine de l’environnement, dont au moins une année en gestion de projets.

Expérience de projets d’assainissement des sols et des eaux souterraines, notamment en délimitation, en surveillance et en gestion.
Expérience dans la sélection et la direction de sous-traitants.
Expérience en facturation, en budgétisation et dans d’autres volets de la gestion de projets.
Capacité démontrée à gérer et à diriger efficacement le personnel de terrain.
Excellentes aptitudes à communiquer oralement et par écrit en français; une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais constitue un atout.
Expérience en communication avec les clients, les organismes de réglementation et les autres parties prenantes.
Permis de conduire valide et disponibilité pour se déplacer dans la province de Québec.

Milieu et conditions de trava il

Nous accueillons et encourageons les candidatures de personnes en situation de handicap. Des mesures d’adaptation sont offertes sur demande aux personnes candidates tout au long du processus de recrutement et d’évaluation.

Veuillez noter que nous ne verserons aucuns frais pour un placement découlant de la réception d’un curriculum vitæ non sollicité et que tout curriculum vitæ ainsi transmis sera considéré comme de l’information publique. Nous acceptons volontiers les curriculum vitæ soumis directement par les personnes candidates.

With offices across Canada, Pario Engineering & Environmental Sciences LP is a niche forensic engineering, environmental science, and remediation consulting firm that is a leader in providing services to insurance and risk management clients.

We have an existing opening for a Project Manager to join our Quebec City team. This position will support our growing Quebec operations, which provide environmental science and project management services to the insurance and risk management markets. The position will involve working with clients and team members to direct spill mitigation, delineation, remediation, and documentation to support clean ups and file closure.

Role Requirements:
Degree in Science or Engineering (Environmental or Earth Sciences preferred) or related diploma with applicable experience.
A minimum of 5 years’ experience within the environmental field with at least 1 year of project management experience.

Experience in soil and groundwater remediation projects including delineation, monitoring and management.
Experience retaining and directing subcontractors.
Experience with invoicing, budgeting, and other areas of project management.
Successfully managing and directing field staff is a must.
Strong verbal and written communication skills in French, strong English communication is an asset.
Experience communicating with clients, regulators and other involved stakeholders.
A valid driver's license and willingness to travel within the province of Quebec.

Environment/Work Conditions

We welcome and encourage applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates throughout the recruitment and assessment process.
